merge.title: Fail-stop memory integrity: MSPLIM with a re-basing fault trampoline, a decoded and region-scoped ECC NMI, secrets in an ECC-on secure bank, and the SRAM option bits pinned into the ship profile before RDP-2 freezes them
merge.threat: Three silent-corruption classes with no detector today. (1) Stack overflow: no image programs MSPLIM/PSPLIM (the only hits in fsbl/, secure/, nonsecure/ are two comments, fsbl/src/main.rs:172 and fsbl/src/manifest.rs:30). The secure stack grows down from the top of the 192 K SRAM1 window (secure/memory-stm32u585.x:31-35) straight into .bss, where `static mut STATE` holds master_secret and SLOT_CACHE (secure/src/nsc/state.rs:542). Companion-shaped parsers (ERC-7730, EIP-712, multiSend, typed-call) run on that stack and its worst case is unproven (#374). (2) Bit flips: secrets live in SRAM1, and per #48 only SRAM2 and part of SRAM3 are ECC-capable, so SRAM1 has no ECC at all. A laser/EM flip in key material or signing state is invisible; the double-compute compare only catches faults that differ between the two passes (SLasH-DSA, arXiv 2509.13048). (3) Remanence: the software boot scrub covers named caches only and is skipped on Cold and OptionByte resets (secure/src/main.rs:1311-1333, secure/src/reset_cause.rs:66-112); stack residue (entropy temporaries, C10 scratch) is never wiped; the hardware erase bit that covers the secret bank (SRAM_RST) is not set by any recipe (Makefile:364-380 sets SRAM2_RST, the NS bank).
merge.proposal:
Four phases, ordered by irreversibility.

PHASE 0 — option bits, before any die runs the RDP-2 self-lock. Add SRAM_RST=0 (hardware erase of SRAM1/3/4 on system reset), SRAM2_RST=0, and the ECC bit for whichever bank holds secrets (SRAM3_ECC and/or SRAM2_ECC, active-low per #48) to:
- the ship option-byte profile;
- `ObField` and the Phase A verifier, which today check only BootLock, OemLock, Rdp, SecBootAdd0, Secwm1/2, SwapBank, Tzen, Wrp1a/2a (secure/src/first_boot/state.rs; shared/src/lockdown.rs has only an advisory BOR decode at :517-521);
- the RDP-0 pre-power SWD check.
RDP-2 freezes these forever, so a die locked without them can never gain hardware SRAM erase or ECC. Confirm bit positions and polarity on a sacrificial board (#82, #46).

PHASE 1 — MSPLIM (small).
- Secure world: first instructions of reset/pre_init set MSPLIM_S = end of .bss/.uninit (`__sheap`) plus a 256 B guard. The limit must not be ORIGIN(RAM); the thing to protect is STATE in .bss.
- HardFault needs a naked trampoline that re-bases MSP to `_stack_start` (or zeroes MSPLIM) before any Rust runs. The current handler (secure/src/main.rs:4682-4690) calls `zeroize_sensitive_state` through `with_state` closures on a stack already at the limit; a second STKOF at HardFault priority risks lockup with secrets still resident. Trezor does exactly this re-base (systask.c:823-840).
- At NS handover set MSPLIM_NS (secure/src/boot_ns.rs:19-77 sets only MSP_NS/PSP_NS). This is DoS hygiene only; NS owns that register.
- FSBL: MSPLIM belongs in the replacement FSBL's guard policy (#542 FA-2.0/2.1). Clear it before `bx` in fsbl/src/branch.rs:76-92 (already a P2 port at docs/architecture/trezor-comparison.md:645).
- CI: assert guard + worst-case bound < static_end..stack_start, fed by #374's cargo-call-stack result.

PHASE 2 — NMI decode.
- Secure NMI handler reads FLASH_ECCR (ECCD, address, bank) and the RAMCFG ISR/FEAR registers, clears the flags, then zeroizes and resets.
- A double error inside per-device data pages 123-127 must take a defined fail-safe path (treat the quadword as torn, or halt with a fatal code), not a blind reset loop. This is #94's undecided branch.
- FSBL gets an NMI handler with Trezor's region rule: fatal only if the address is inside the FSBL's own range; a double error inside a slot marks that slot invalid so the other slot can still boot.

PHASE 3 — ECC-on secret bank.
- Dedicated linker section for STATE, the SE driver caches, OptRand/shuffle seeds and signing scratch, placed in the ECC-capable part of SRAM3 and kept secure via MPCBB3. Not SRAM2: that is the NS world's RAM today (nonsecure/memory-stm32u585.x:9; secure/src/sau.rs:436-440 sets MPCBB2 all non-secure).
- Enable RAMCFG ECC with double-error routed to NMI and single-error counts readable for telemetry.
- Prerequisites: secure RAMCFG first (#150, it is NS-attributed today); zero-fill the region at boot before first use if RM0456 requires initialised ECC RAM (to confirm).

PHASE 4 — remanence residue (small).
- Volatile clear of the unused stack below SP on lock, idle-wipe, panic/HardFault/NMI, and before `bxns`.
- Extend the boot scrub to run on every reset cause, including Cold.

members.note: Kept: (1) MSPLIM and (2) ECC bank + double-error NMI. Round-1 confirmed nothing is implemented and no decision contradicts it. Corrections applied: SRAM2 is not available as the secret bank (it is NS RAM); #150 is a prerequisite; the limit goes at the end of .bss. Parts (3) page-123 tag, (4) page-124 encoding and (5) Kani fault models are moved out of this cluster to #93/#230/#397; see dropped_parts.

Backbone of the merge. No round-1 verdict, so I checked it. Confirmed: no MSPLIM/PSPLIM/RAMCFG/ECC code in any image; the NMI handler exists (secure/src/main.rs:4651). Corrected: (a) the existing HardFault cannot be reused unchanged on a limit-exhausted stack; (c) the target bank is SRAM3, not SRAM2; (d) 'arm flash ECCD' becomes 'decode and region-scope', because ECCD very likely already raises NMI; the Trezor precedent 'pins SRAM3 ECC in OPTR' is probably inverted (see precedent). P0 downgraded to P1: no production build can exist while the S-2 fence stands. (e) stays with #374.

No round-1 verdict; checked. Confirmed: no MSPLIM anywhere; boot_ns.rs sets only MSP_NS/PSP_NS; no UsageFault handler, so STKOF escalates to HardFault. Trezor precedent confirmed (systask.c:170 `stack_base + 256`; sysutils.c:94). Corrected: 'keep the existing HardFault' is unsafe without an MSP re-base; 'stack_base + 256' has no meaning here because there is no dedicated stack region, so the limit is end-of-.bss plus guard; FSBL MSPLIM goes into the replacement FSBL, not the legacy 32 KiB bench image; the FSBL fault handler adds bytes against the FSBL budget.

No round-1 verdict; checked. Kept: clear unused stack on lock/fault/handoff; hardware SRAM erase in the ship profile. Corrected: (4) names the wrong bit, SRAM2_RST erases the NS bank and the secret bank needs SRAM_RST (secure/src/reset_cause.rs:96-98, #82); the 'zero hits, only named-cache wipes' evidence understates what exists, a reset-cause-gated boot scrub is present (main.rs:1311-1333) and the real gap is named-state-only plus skipped on Cold. Dropped: FSBL random-then-zero fill, wipe-all-secure-SRAM before NS, BKP clear, temperature floor.

dropped_parts: FI-10(3) DHUK-rooted tag over the page-123 live set, as written: it does not detect its own stated threat. Dropping the newest record together with its tag leaves the previous record/tag pair valid, so a one-commit rollback verifies. It also doubles the 16 B/increment log cost and, per established fact (d), any secure-world code can recompute a DHUK tag. Design it with #93 (per-quadword integrity) and #230 (generation marker).

FI-10(4) Hamming-structured page-124 marker: moved to #397 at P3, not refuted. SE050 enforces the 10-attempt bound in silicon, and a page forced to read blank while E120 has advanced trips the boot wipe (`E120_used > page124_used`, CLAUDE.md invariant #2), so the result is fail-secure DoS, not extra PIN attempts. Round-1 also showed the encoding needs an 'initialised' header record because the page is legitimately all-0xFF after every successful unlock (secure/src/hw/flash.rs:779).
FI-10(5) Kani/rainbow stuck-at models for the page-123/124 decoders: counter-integrity work, extend #397 instead of opening a parallel harness.

FI-10 / SYS-03(c) 'place secrets in SRAM2': not available without evicting the NS world. NS links at 0x2003_0000/64 K (nonsecure/memory-stm32u585.x:9) and MPCBB2 is all non-secure (secure/src/sau.rs:436-440). Use the ECC part of SRAM3.

SYS-03(d) / #248 'arm the flash ECCD NMI': replaced. ECCD very likely needs no enable (Trezor handles it inside NMI and sets no enable bit anywhere in core/embed). The work is decoding and scoping, not arming.

SYS-09(1) FSBL TRNG-random-then-zero fill of all SRAM: the FSBL has no TRNG and its size and boot time are the recorded NO-GO budget (a-b-firmware-rollback-architecture, memory note project_ab_rollback_spec_review). SRAM_RST=0 gives a hardware erase on every system reset at zero flash cost. A zero-only fill remains only if ECC RAM turns out to need initialisation.

SYS-09(2) wipe all secure SRAM before branching to NS: contradicts the architecture. STATE must survive across NSC calls, and NS cannot read secure SRAM anyway (MPCBB1 all secure, sau.rs:428-433). Only the unused-stack clear survives.

SYS-09(3) clear non-BHK TAMP backup registers at handoff: no secret is shown to live there. BKP0R..7R hold the BHK and must stay, and they are reloaded from page 126 each boot (established fact c). No threat is closed.
SYS-09(5) temperature floor against frozen-SRAM attacks: belongs to the SYS-01 cluster (HARDENING.md §4.7 states it as a requirement only). Not evaluated here.
SYS-09(4) SRAM2_RST=0 as the remanence control: wrong bank. Kept only as a companion bit; SRAM_RST=0 is the load-bearing one (#82).

USB-03 'install an FSBL HardFault handler with a distinctive LCD pattern' in the legacy bench FSBL: the 32 KiB bench linker is legacy and the pq1 FSBL cannot light the panel at all (#705). Fold into the replacement FSBL's guard/fault policy (#542).
USB-03 'MSPLIM as the first instruction of main': too late. cortex-m-rt's pre-main init has already run on an unguarded stack; set it in the reset path / pre_init.
SYS-03 risk note 'ECC double-error NMI during a flash write must not corrupt the journal (extend TLA+)': kept only as a prerequisite pointer to #542 FA-2.2/2.3; no new work proposed here.

No issue names any of these:
1. Programming the MSPLIM register in the secure world, with the limit at end-of-.bss rather than a 'stack base'.
2. The naked HardFault trampoline that re-bases MSP before the zeroize path. Without it, MSPLIM can turn an overflow into a lockup with secrets resident.
3. MSPLIM_NS at handover, and MSPLIM clear in fsbl/src/branch.rs.
4. Adding SRAM_RST, SRAM2_RST and the SRAM ECC bits to `ObField` / the Phase A verifier / the RDP-0 pre-power check. #82 and #248 only touch the bench Makefile recipe.
5. Decoding FLASH_ECCR in the existing NMI handler and the FSBL region-scoping rule. #94 asks only for a silicon determination.
6. The fact that SRAM2 is the NS bank, so #48's suggested placement needs an SRAM3/MPCBB3 design.
7. Unused-stack clear, and the boot scrub skipping Cold resets.
8. Doc and comment corrections: docs/security/brownout-hardening.md:321 says ECC is 'always active' on SRAM1/2/3; secure/src/main.rs:4643 says no NMI source is armed.
decision_conflicts: No recorded owner decision is contradicted by the kept parts. The Trezor critical-port memory note declines only the secmon port.

Invariant #10 / RDP-2 freezes option bytes: the ECC and SRAM_RST bits must enter the single ship profile before any self-lock. The bank choice (Phase 3) therefore has to be decided before Phase 0 can be frozen; that ordering is an owner decision.

A/B rollback architecture, FSBL size and boot budget is the NO-GO: FSBL-side additions (MSPLIM, NMI handler) must be costed inside the replacement FSBL's 40 KiB registry (#540/#542), not added to the legacy image. The FSBL random fill is dropped for this reason.
Secure slot is already 76,949 B over with ui-px: Phases 1, 2 and 4 are tens to low hundreds of bytes; Phase 3 moves data, not code, but touches the linker scripts and SAU/MPCBB tables.
CLAUDE.md 'no new per-signature flash state beyond page 123' and the 16 B/increment format: the reason the page-123 tag is not carried here.
Invariant #2 (SE silicon is the PIN authority): the reason the page-124 encoding is demoted to P3.

merge.precedent:
Trezor ships the software half of all of this.
- MSPLIM at reset: core/embed/sys/startup/stm32u5/startup_init.c:336 (`_stack_section_start + 128`); per-stack programming at core/embed/sys/startup/stm32/sysutils.c:94; disabled at stage handoff at sysutils.c:289 and :327; per-task `sp_lim = stack_base + 256` at core/embed/sys/task/stm32/systask.c:170.
- STKOF-aware fault entry that re-bases MSP: systask.c:823-840.
- Flash ECCD decoded inside NMI with region scoping in boardloader and bootloader: systask.c:877-900.
- Unused-stack clear and RAM fill: startup_init.c:349, :365-367; core/embed/sys/startup/stm32/bootutils.c:115-121, :152-158, :257-266.

Correction to SYS-03's precedent: option_bytes.c:79-82 sets the FLASH_OPTR_SRAM3_ECC and FLASH_OPTR_SRAM_RST bits to 1. Under the active-low polarity recorded in #48, that means SRAM3 ECC disabled and no hardware erase of SRAM1/3 on reset; Trezor relies on the software fill instead. I could not confirm polarity from the local Trezor tree (the vendored ST header is not checked out), so treat this as likely, not certain. A grep for RAMCFG in core/embed finds only backup-RAM use, so Trezor does not appear to route an SRAM ECC NMI. Ledger: nothing verifiable (closed SE firmware).
merge.rationale:
Priority is P1, not SYS-03's P0: no production image can be built while the S-2 fence stands, so nothing here is exploitable in a shipped unit today. It is not P2 either, because Phase 0 has a hard deadline. The first-boot self-lock freezes option bytes, and the verifier that gates that lock does not look at any SRAM erase or ECC bit.

Cost is M overall: Phases 1, 2 and 4 are small firmware changes; Phase 0 is mostly ceremony and a sacrificial-board run; Phase 3 is the real work (linker section, MPCBB3, RAMCFG, #150).

Kind is mixed because half the value is the option-byte profile and its verification, which is process, not code.

Phase 1 alone is worth doing first: it is the only available stack-overflow detector in a Rust no_std image, and it converts #374's unproven bound from silent corruption of STATE into fail-stop.

live_defects.what: The secure NMI handler zeroizes and resets without reading or clearing FLASH_ECCR, and the FSBL has no NMI handler at all (panic-halt plus cortex-m-rt defaults). If a double-ECC flash read raises NMI, a torn quadword in page 123/124 becomes a reset loop, and a damaged slot page halts the FSBL even when the other slot is good.
live_defects.evidence: secure/src/main.rs:4636-4656 (handler; comment 'today NO NMI source is armed'); fsbl/src/main.rs:76-78 and fsbl/Cargo.toml:131 (panic-halt, no exception handlers found in fsbl/src); Trezor handles ECCD inside NMI with no enable bit (core/embed/sys/task/stm32/systask.c:877-900); #94 records the silicon behaviour as undetermined.
live_defects.reachable_in_production_config: Conditional. Depends on whether STM32U585 raises NMI on a double-ECC flash read (believed yes per RM0456, not re-read here, not measured on silicon). If yes it is reachable by a power cut during a page-123/124 program on any build.

live_defects.what: The ship option-byte verifier does not cover SRAM_RST, SRAM2_RST, SRAM2_ECC or SRAM3_ECC, and BOR is advisory only. The RDP-2 self-lock would freeze whatever the factory left, including defaults with no hardware SRAM erase and no ECC.
live_defects.evidence: ObField variants used in secure/src/first_boot/state.rs are BootLock, OemLock, Rdp, SecBootAdd0, Secwm1, Secwm2, SwapBank, Tzen, Wrp1a, Wrp2a; shared/src/lockdown.rs:517-521 (BOR decode 'not yet a hard gate'); grep for SRAM/ECC in secure/src/first_boot returns nothing.
live_defects.reachable_in_production_config: Not yet. `rdp2-self-lock` is a production-quarantined candidate and `mode-production + optiga-trust-m` is compile-fenced by OPTIGA_S2_PRODUCTION_BLOCKED. It becomes permanent per die the moment that path ships.
live_defects.severity: High once the self-lock ships (irreversible per die); none today

live_defects.what: The only recipe that sets a RAM-erase option bit sets the wrong bank: SRAM2_RST erases the NS world's RAM, while secrets live in SRAM1.
live_defects.evidence: Makefile:364-380 (`--optionbytes BOR_LEV=3 SRAM2_RST=0`); secure/src/reset_cause.rs:96-98; secure/memory-stm32u585.x:31 (secure RAM at 0x3000_0000, 192 K); nonsecure/memory-stm32u585.x:9 (NS RAM at 0x2003_0000, 64 K). Already known as #82.
live_defects.reachable_in_production_config: Bench recipe only; the ship profile has no such bit at all (see previous defect).

live_defects.what: Two statements in the repo are wrong or in doubt and will mislead the next reader: brownout-hardening says single-bit ECC is 'always active, no config needed' on SRAM1/2/3; the NMI handler comment says no NMI source is armed.
live_defects.evidence: docs/security/brownout-hardening.md:321 versus #48 (ECC is an option bit, off by default, SRAM2 and part of SRAM3 only); secure/src/main.rs:4643 versus the ECCD point above. Round-1 already flagged the first.

live_defects.what: The boot-time secret scrub wipes named caches only and is skipped on Cold and OptionByte resets; stack residue is never cleared on any path.
live_defects.evidence: secure/src/main.rs:1311-1333; secure/src/reset_cause.rs:66-112 (`requires_secret_scrub` = abnormal or Software); secure/src/nsc/mod.rs:1729-1744 (`zeroize_sensitive_state` touches STATE and the SE caches only).
live_defects.reachable_in_production_config: Yes on any build, but exploitation needs physical SRAM readout after a fast power cycle; startup re-zeroes .bss, so the exposed data is stack residue.

merge.residual_after:
What an attacker can still do once all four phases land:
- Fault registers, the instruction stream, or peripheral data paths (HASH, SAES, I2C). ECC covers stored bits only.
- Inject a matched double-bit flip that produces a valid codeword, or repeat the same fault in both signing passes; ECC plus double-compute raises the cost but does not close SLasH-DSA-class faults.
- Overflow within the guard: a single frame larger than 256 B can step over the guard without touching it between probes. MSPLIM checks SP updates, so this is caught only if the limit is exact and #374's bound holds.
- Use the fail-stop as a DoS: every induced fault is now a deterministic reset. This is accepted policy (reset, not SE wipe).
- Read SRAM invasively on a powered, unlocked device (probing, not reset-based remanence). SRAM_RST and stack clears do nothing against that.
- Recover data from flash pages 123-127 or roll the page-123 tally back by one record; counter integrity is not addressed here (#93/#230).
- Any die locked to RDP-2 before Phase 0 keeps its original option bits forever.
- NS can still clear MSPLIM_NS and crash itself.

skeptic.reason:
The core survives: no image programs a stack limit, the ship option-byte verifier ignores every SRAM erase/ECC bit, and the NMI path neither decodes nor scopes a flash double-ECC error. I confirmed each by reading the code. No recorded owner decision is contradicted.

Six parts of the merge are wrong or weaker than stated; none sinks it, but Phase 3 and Phase 4 need rewriting.

1. **Phase 3 protects the wrong object.** It moves STATE and named caches to an ECC bank but leaves the stack in SRAM1. The signing computation (entropy reconstruction, C10 secret seeds, WOTS/FORS scratch, the double-compute buffers) runs on the stack, so the stated bit-flip threat is mostly untouched.
2. **The Trezor precedent is inverted on the bank question.** Trezor's secret RAM is SRAM2: `MAIN_RAM_START = 0x30030000` (core/embed/models/T3T1/memory.ld:42), and secmon.ld:67-69 says .data/.bss sit there because SRAM2 "is cleared on security events". Its OPTR value leaves SRAM2_ECC and SRAM2_RST at 0 (option_bytes.c:78-84), which is enabled under the active-low polarity from #48. The merge said Trezor relies on software fill and dismissed SRAM2.
3. **Phase 4's "extend the boot scrub to Cold" is a no-op.** STATE is in .bss (secure/src/nsc/state.rs:539-542) and cortex-m-rt zeroes .bss on every reset before main. The only real residue is stack and .uninit.
4. **The "lockup with secrets resident" risk is overstated.** `iwdg` is in PROD_SHIP_FEATURES (Makefile:2718) with a ~2 s timeout (secure/src/hw/iwdg.rs:108-117), so a lockup is bounded to about 1-3 s before a watchdog reset and .bss re-zero. The trampoline is still the right design.
5. **The "frame larger than 256 B steps over the guard" residual is wrong.** MSPLIM is a comparison on SP updates and exception stacking, not a guard page; a large `sub sp` faults.
6. **Existing mechanisms were missed.** cortex-m-rt 0.7.5 (Cargo.lock:338) already provides `_stack_end = __euninit` (link.x.in:189) and the `zero-init-ram` and `paint-stack` features.

Bypass residual after the corrected plan: faults on registers, the instruction stream and peripherals; identical faults in both signing passes; invasive probing of a powered, unlocked unit; deterministic reset as DoS.

skeptic.corrections:
1. **Phase 3, redesign.** Do not build a dedicated section for STATE only. Put the whole secure RAM region (.data, .bss and stack) in an ECC bank. Two options for the owner:
   - (a) Relink secure RAM into the ECC part of SRAM3 (secure alias 0x3004_0000; ECC span to confirm in RM0456) and program MPCBB3. This is a one-line memory.x change plus an MPCBB table, and it covers the stack.
   - (b) Follow Trezor: swap banks so secure uses SRAM2 (ECC, SRAM2_RST, and hardware erase on tamper, which matters because `tamp`/`tamp-wipe` are forced on for shipping) and NS moves to SRAM1 or SRAM3. This needs the secure world to fit in 64 K, which is unknown until #374. It also changes the SAU NS-SRAM window (secure/src/sau.rs:49-51) and the proto NS_SRAM pointer-validation window, both under const asserts.
   - The bank choice gates Phase 0.

2. **Precedent, fix.** Trezor does use an ECC, reset-erased bank for secrets, and that bank is SRAM2. Only SRAM3 ECC and SRAM_RST are left off. Trezor also marks RAMCFG secure and privileged (core/embed/sec/trustzone/stm32u5/tz_init.c:269-271), which is direct precedent for #150.

3. **Phase 4, rewrite.**
   - Drop "extend the boot scrub to Cold"; .bss is already zeroed on every reset.
   - Replace with cortex-m-rt's `zero-init-ram` feature, which zeroes `_ram_start.._ram_end` including the stack region at startup. This also satisfies any ECC-RAM initialisation requirement. Add SRAM_RST=0 on top.
   - Keep the volatile unused-stack clear on lock, idle wipe and fault.
   - "Before bxns" is ambiguous. Specify: once at boot handover, and optionally on NSC return bounded by a high-water mark. A full clear on every gateway return is avoidable cost.

4. **Phase 1, adjust.**
   - Use the existing `_stack_end` symbol; no custom `__sheap` arithmetic is needed.
   - The Trezor re-base cited at systask.c:823-840 is in `UsageFault_Handler`, not HardFault. pq1 has no UsageFault handler, so STKOF escalates to HardFault.
   - Either enable UsageFault and re-base there, or use a naked HardFault trampoline. The cheap fallback is CCR.STKOFHFNMIGN=1, at the price of the handler's own frames descending into .bss while it wipes.
   - State the lockup risk as bounded by the ~2 s IWDG, not as indefinite secret residency.
   - QEMU mps2-an505 models MSPLIM, so a fault test can run in `make e2e` before any silicon work.

5. **Residual, fix.** Delete the "frame larger than the guard skips it" item. The true residual is SP-relative writes below SP without an SP update, and the limit being checked on MSP only.

6. **Phase 2, tighten.**
   - FLASH_ECCR resets with the system, so the current zeroize-and-reset handler does not wedge on a stale flag. The brick case is a persistent double error in a page read on every boot (123/124), giving a reset loop.
   - The handler must record the address before reset, or the loop is undiagnosable on a board with no LCD.
   - The FSBL has no exception handlers at all, so an NMI lands in cortex-m-rt's default infinite loop, and the FSBL has no watchdog. Scope this to the replacement FSBL (#542) as the merge says.

7. **Phase 0, add.**
   - `ob_field_code` in secure/src/first_boot/state.rs:150 is an exhaustive match, so new ObField variants force new FirstBootError codes and doc updates.
   - The option-byte write path itself is the known-defective #268 (control bits written to SECCR instead of NSCR).
   - Nothing in secure/ or nonsecure/ relies on SRAM surviving reset (no .uninit or noinit use found), so SRAM_RST=0 has no functional conflict.

8. **Tracked issues.**
   - The list is accurate; all states check out.
   - #484 is CLOSED and belongs in the list, not only in prerequisites.
   - #544 (sacrificial-silicon campaign, owner-gated) is the real gate for the hardware asks and should be in the list.
   - #545 is the campaign tracker for #540/#542.
   - #248's title is "TAMP + CSS + PVD"; the ECC/RAMCFG content is in its body, and `#21-tamp-css_pvd` in the NMI comment is the same item.

9. **Docs.** docs/security/brownout-hardening.md:314-315 also says IWDG is disabled and has no code, which is stale: hw/iwdg.rs exists and the feature is in the ship set. Add it to the doc-fix list beside line 321.

10. **Cost.** L for the whole cluster (Phase 3, #150, #374 and sacrificial silicon); Phase 1 alone is S. Suggest splitting it: Phase 1 as its own P1/S item, Phase 0 as a P1 process item gated on the bank decision.

11. **Live defects, verdicts.**
   - (1) NMI not decoded, FSBL has no NMI handler: CONFIRMED, conditional on ECCD raising NMI. See `live_defect`.
   - (2) Verifier ignores SRAM bits: CONFIRMED. ObField (shared/src/lockdown.rs:295-312) has no SRAM, ECC or BOR variant. Not reachable today.
   - (3) Wrong bank in the bench recipe: CONFIRMED (Makefile:364-380, `SRAM2_RST=0` only). Tracked as #82.
   - (4) Doc and comment drift: CONFIRMED (brownout-hardening.md:321; secure/src/main.rs:4643), plus the stale IWDG row.
   - (5) Boot scrub skipped on Cold: PARTLY DENIED. The skip is real (main.rs:1331, reset_cause.rs:110-112) but harmless, since .bss is zeroed at every startup. Only the stack-residue half stands: Low, needs physical readout.

The option-byte additions must land in the single ship profile before any RDP-2 self-lock (invariant #10), so the bank decision is an owner decision that gates Phase 0.

A Trezor-style SRAM2 swap would change the NS RAM window (secure/src/sau.rs:49-51 and the proto NS_SRAM pointer-validation window, both const-asserted) and the NS linker script. That touches invariant #4's validation surface and needs its own review.
FSBL-side work must be costed in the replacement FSBL (#540/#542), not the legacy 32 KiB image; the FSBL budget is the recorded NO-GO.
The secure slot is already 76,949 B over with ui-px. A naked trampoline, an NMI decode and a stack clear are small, but any added code competes for the same unresolved flash lever.
